verdict: MARKOV CHAIN ON THE DIRECTED NETWORK. 9,171 of 191,447 PPI edges (4.79%) carry an evidence-backed arrow, so at most one transition in twenty is constrained and a small effect was predicted in advance. MEASURED on the standing harness: UNDIR 0.4736, DIR 0.4679 (-0.0056 +/- 0.0023, WORSE), DIR-REV 0.4712, DIR-SHUF 0.4772. DIRECTION DOES NOT HELP THIS TASK. DIR vs DIR-REV is -0.0033 +/- 0.0028 (indistinguishable) -- reversing every arrow costs nothing measurable, which means any difference from UNDIR comes from making edges one-way rather than from the arrows pointing the right way. THE LIKELY REASON EITHER WAY is coverage, not correctness: the arrows are 0.83-accurate but touch under 5% of edges, and the walk's mass is dominated by the 95% that stay symmetric. Nothing here contradicts edge_direction.py's separate result that a walk cannot INFER direction -- that was about reading direction OUT of the graph; this is about feeding measured direction IN.
